title: Opening a tab or coming from another page starts at the top-left
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. at least 8 technicians (as in the scroll test)). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (about 20 work orders led by one technician (e.g. Esther Howard) so the board and table scroll both ways):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose a customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Scroll the board right and scroll down inside a long column.
  5. Click the Estimates tab, then click the All tab.
  6. Note where the board is scrolled to.
  7. Scroll right and down again.
  8. Click Schedule in the top navigation, then click Work Orders in the top navigation.
  9. Note where the board is scrolled to.
  10. Scroll right and down again.
  11. While still on Board View, click Work Orders in the top navigation.
  12. Note where the board is scrolled to.
  13. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  14. Repeat steps 4 to 12 in Tech View (scroll down and right in the table).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • After clicking a tab the board starts at the top and all the way to the left: Unassigned and the first technicians are in view and every column starts at its first card.
  • Coming back from Schedule through the Work Orders link it also starts at the top-left.
  • Clicking Work Orders in the top navigation while already on Board View does not leave the page, so the board keeps exactly the scroll position you had.
  • Tech View behaves the same way: top-left after a tab click or coming from another page, unchanged after clicking Work Orders while already on Tech View.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-R12, read 8 Oct 2026. PO decision Chris Ward, PRD footer comment 6 Oct 2026, item 6 (header click keeps the place).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R12: “In Tech View and Board View, opening a filter view any way other than browser Back (for example clicking its tab, a link, or a menu item) starts scrolled to the top and all the way to the left. List behaves as it does today. Clicking “Work Orders” in the header while already on Tech View or Board View does not leave the page, so it keeps the current scroll position, as the List does.”
